choices.explanation: These are necessary conditions other than routing.

choices.text: Look only at the CIDR and do not check the port or listener
choices.explanation: Correct. The CIDR alone does not satisfy the connection requirements.

learning.concept: Why a public IPv4 address alone does not enable connectivity
learning.reason: A subnet name alone cannot determine the route. Check the route, communication permissions, and the listener at the destination.

questions.title: Layer Exposure Scope
questions.prompt: An architect is placing three tiers—a public web tier, an internal application tier, and a database tier—in a VPC. Only the web tier should accept direct connections from the internet. Select two incorrect judgments regarding this requirement.

choices.text: Place only the necessary entry points on public routes and design the outbound requirements of the other tiers separately
choices.explanation: It is appropriate to limit the public entry points and consider outbound communication for internal tiers separately.

choices.text: A security group is unnecessary if an IGW route exists
choices.explanation: Routing and communication permissions are separate conditions.

choices.text: The name private alone can prevent external access
choices.explanation: Routes, addresses, and permissions must be checked.

choices.text: Provide public routes for the web tier and allow only the necessary internal communication for the database tier.
choices.explanation: This limits direct user connections to the web tier and avoids exposing the database tier.

learning.concept: Limit public exposure to the necessary entry points
learning.reason: Limit internet reachability to the web tier, and design outbound communication for internal tiers and communication permissions for each tier separately.

units.title: Diagnose VPC connectivity through routes and control points
units.summary: Determine the route that matches the destination, then examine in order the path to the internet and the rules that allow communication.
units.objective: For communication within and outside a VPC, verify the route, permission for the source and destination, and return traffic with supporting evidence.
explanation: A route determines the next hop toward the destination. Reaching it also requires a return path, as well as the conditions imposed by the Security Group, Network ACL, and services along the path.
units.example: When an EC2 instance in a private subnet cannot retrieve external updates, check in order the default route to the NAT, the IGW route in the NAT’s public subnet, and permission for the source and destination.

learningObjectives.text: Determine the selected route from the destination IP address and the longest-prefix match.
Distinguish the traffic handled by the IGW and NAT Gateway from their placement.
Explain the scope of application of Security Groups and Network ACLs, and the conditions required to return a response.
When a connection cannot be established within or between VPCs, verify name resolution, the round-trip path, and the rules that allow communication.

sections.title: Determine the next hop from the destination
paragraphs: A VPC route table associates destination CIDRs or prefix lists with targets, which are the next hops. The initial route table contains a local route for traffic within the VPC. To communicate with a VPC peering connection, add a route whose destination is the peer's address range.
When multiple routes match, the longest prefix match—that is, the most specific CIDR—is selected. For 10.1.2.3, 10.1.0.0/16 takes precedence over 10.0.0.0/8.
A one-way route alone cannot support bidirectional communication such as TCP. For VPC peering, VPNs, and other VPCs, also check the route back from the peer to the source.

example.scenario: An EC2 instance at 10.0.2.0/24 cannot connect to 10.1.0.10 in a peered VPC.
steps: Check the target matching 10.1.0.10 in the source subnet's route table.
Check the route back to 10.0.2.0/24 in the peer VPC.
Check permissions on both sides and the service at the destination.
example.outcome: You can diagnose the issue based on the destination and return CIDRs instead of relying only on the default route.

misconception.claim: A 0.0.0.0/0 route guarantees reachability to any private CIDR.
misconception.correction: The target of a default route may not know that private CIDR. A target appropriate for the destination and a bidirectional path are required.

takeaways: Choose the most specific route for the destination IP.
A return route is also a condition for communication.

sections.title: The path in from the internet and the path out
paragraphs: An internet gateway (IGW) attaches to a VPC and serves as the target for internet-bound traffic in the route table. To make an EC2 instance reachable from outside over IPv4, you need a route to the IGW, a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP, and the required permissions.

An EC2 instance in a private subnet can initiate traffic such as retrieving update files through a public NAT gateway. The diagram shows a per-Availability Zone design. The private subnet's default route points to the NAT gateway, and the default route of the public subnet containing the NAT points to the IGW.

A NAT gateway is not a device for accepting new SSH connections from outside to a private EC2 instance. Do not declare an outage solely because the NAT gateway's IP cannot be pinged; check its available state, the two routes, and the source and destination permissions.

example.scenario: In a design using a public NAT gateway per Availability Zone, an EC2 instance in a private subnet cannot connect to the OS update destination.
steps: Check whether 0.0.0.0/0 in the private subnet targets the NAT gateway.
Check that the NAT gateway is in a public subnet and that 0.0.0.0/0 in that subnet targets the IGW.
Check the EC2 egress rules and external conditions or NACLs that could block return traffic.
example.outcome: You can verify the source, path, and external reachability together instead of stopping after creating the NAT.

misconception.claim: Creating a NAT gateway in a private subnet allows SSH access from outside to EC2 instances in that subnet.
misconception.correction: A NAT is an egress point for traffic initiated from the private side. It is not intended to relay new inbound connections from outside to private EC2 instances.

takeaways: NAT is an egress point for traffic initiated from the private side.
Check the two routes: private subnet → NAT → IGW.

sections.title: The difference between security groups and network ACLs
paragraphs: A security group (SG) is a firewall associated with network interfaces and similar resources. Because it is stateful, responses to allowed traffic pass without adding an allow rule in the reverse direction. For newly initiated traffic, allow only the required peers and ports.

A network ACL (NACL) applies to a subnet. It is stateless and evaluates inbound and outbound traffic separately. Even if a request is allowed, the response does not return unless the ephemeral port used for the response is allowed.
Routes, NACLs, and security groups are not substitutes for one another. Routes handle destinations, NACLs handle subnet boundaries, and security groups handle network interface boundaries.

example.scenario: An HTTPS request reaches a web EC2 instance from an ALB, but the response does not return.
steps: Check both directions for the request and return traffic in the NACLs of the ALB subnet and EC2 subnet.
In the EC2 security group, allow TCP 443 from the ALB's security group.
Check the source and destination routes and whether the service is listening.
example.outcome: You can explain why a NACL's outbound rule cannot be omitted even when a security group is stateful.

misconception.claim: If a security group is stateful, the NACL on the same path automatically allows return traffic.
misconception.correction: A NACL is a stateless filter independent of a security group. NACLs require rules in both directions.

takeaways: SGs are stateful at the network interface boundary.
NACLs are stateless at the subnet boundary.

sections.title: Troubleshoot private connection failures in sequence
paragraphs: When connecting through a VPC endpoint or to a VPC peering connection, first check whether the name resolves to the intended private IP address. If it resolves to another IP address, examining routes or permission rules does not validate the intended path.

Next, check the source subnet's route, the rules on the sending and receiving sides, and the port on which the destination is listening. If the VPC endpoint has a policy, also check whether the calling principal, operation, and target resource are allowed.

Finally, verify the route for the response from the destination back to the source and the reverse-direction rules of the network ACL. Record name-resolution success separately from whether the connection actually succeeds.

example.scenario: An application's EC2 cannot connect to an AWS service through an interface VPC endpoint.
steps: Check whether the service name resolves to the endpoint's private IP address.
Check the source route and security group, the network ACLs along the path, and the permissions on the endpoint side.
Check whether the endpoint policy allows the caller and operation, then reconnect under the same conditions.
example.outcome: You can narrow down the cause by checking name resolution, the path, and rules that deny the connection in sequence.

misconception.claim: Creating a VPC peering connection automatically allows all traffic between both VPCs.
misconception.correction: Even after creating VPC peering, check the routes on both sides, security groups, NACLs, and, if necessary, name-resolution settings.

takeaways: DNS results are a prerequisite for the path to the destination.
Do not forget source permissions and return traffic.

questions.title: The Role of Routes
questions.prompt: A network administrator is reviewing a route table associated with a VPC subnet. What does one route entry in the table map? Select one correct answer.

choices.text: A destination CIDR or prefix list and the target to which packets are sent
choices.explanation: A route determines where packets matching the specified destination range are sent.

choices.text: Only the ports allowed for inbound traffic by a security group
choices.explanation: Ports allowed for inbound traffic are specified by rules such as security group rules.

choices.text: A rule that resolves a DNS name to a public IP address
choices.explanation: DNS is responsible for name resolution.

learning.concept: Route destinations and targets
learning.reason: When the destination matches, traffic is sent to the target of that route.

questions.title: Longest Prefix Match
questions.prompt: An operations administrator is investigating traffic destined for 10.1.2.3 in a VPC with no other matching routes. When the source route table contains 10.0.0.0/8 and 10.1.0.0/16, select one incorrect statement about route selection.

choices.text: The destination 10.1.2.3 is within the range of 10.0.0.0/8.
choices.explanation: 10.0.0.0/8 includes IPv4 addresses whose first 8 bits are 10.

choices.text: The destination 10.1.2.3 is also within the range of 10.1.0.0/16.
choices.explanation: 10.1.0.0/16 includes IPv4 addresses whose first two octets are 10.1.

choices.text: Because the range of 10.0.0.0/8 is broader, the route for 10.0.0.0/8 is used.
choices.explanation: Among matching candidates, the /16 route with the narrower target range is preferred.

learning.concept: Longest prefix match
learning.reason: Both destination ranges match, but the route with the longer /16 prefix is selected.

questions.title: Return Path
questions.prompt: A network administrator is investigating an order API that uses VPC peering. The call reaches the other VPC's subnet, but the caller cannot receive the response. Select two correct items for further investigation.

choices.text: Check whether the other VPC has a return route to the source CIDR.
choices.explanation: Correct. Bidirectional communication requires a return path.

choices.text: Check whether the route table resolves DNS names.
choices.explanation: Name resolution is the responsibility of DNS.

choices.text: Check the security group and network ACL permissions on both sides.
choices.explanation: Correct. Routes and filters are separate control points.

choices.text: Delete the local route.
choices.explanation: There is no need to delete the local route used for communication within the VPC.

learning.concept: Return paths for private connections
learning.reason: Check both the receiving side's return route and the settings that allow communication on both sides.

questions.title: Public IPv4 Address Reachability
questions.prompt: A web administrator wants to directly accept IPv4 HTTPS connections from users on the internet to EC2 in a VPC. Choose two incorrect explanations of the conditions required for reachability from the internet.

choices.text: Add a route to the internet gateway in the subnet's route table.
choices.explanation: A route used for communication with the internet is required.

choices.text: Assign a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP address to EC2.
choices.explanation: This is required to make EC2 directly accessible from the internet over IPv4.

choices.text: Placing a NAT gateway in a private subnet eliminates the need for an internet gateway.
choices.explanation: An internet gateway is required to expose EC2 directly over IPv4 in this configuration.

choices.text: Allow the applicable HTTPS traffic in the security group.
choices.explanation: In addition to configuring the route, allow the required traffic.

choices.text: Even if only a private IPv4 address is assigned to EC2, the internet gateway automatically performs the translation.
choices.explanation: Direct IPv4 communication requires a corresponding public IPv4 address or Elastic IP address on EC2.

learning.concept: IPv4 internet connectivity to EC2
learning.reason: EC2 requires a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP, and the subnet requires a route to the internet gateway. Also verify the settings that allow the traffic.

questions.title: NAT Scope
questions.prompt: An operations administrator wants an EC2 instance without a public IPv4 address to connect to a distribution source on the internet and retrieve update files. Choose one correct use of a public NAT gateway.

choices.text: Initiate a new SSH connection from outside to EC2.
choices.explanation: A NAT gateway can be used for outbound communication initiated from the private subnet side, such as EC2.

choices.text: Use it as the exit point for outbound communication initiated by EC2.
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: Make all security group rules unnecessary.
choices.explanation: NAT does not replace the permission mechanism.

learning.concept: Outbound communication from a private subnet
learning.reason: Communication initiated by EC2 can exit to the internet through a public NAT gateway and an internet gateway.

questions.title: NAT Routing
questions.prompt: An operations administrator is investigating why an external API cannot be reached from EC2 in a private subnet through a public NAT gateway deployed per Availability Zone. Choose one incorrect interpretation of the clues.

choices.text: Check whether the private subnet's default route points to the NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: A route is required to send packets from EC2 to the NAT gateway.

choices.text: Check whether the public subnet containing the NAT gateway has a route to the internet gateway.
choices.explanation: A route is required for traffic to leave the NAT gateway and reach the internet.

choices.text: Conclude that the NAT gateway has failed solely because it does not respond to ping.
choices.explanation: The NAT gateway itself does not respond to ping. Check its operational status, the routes, and traffic permissions.

learning.concept: Investigating routes through a NAT gateway
learning.reason: You cannot use ping to the NAT gateway itself to verify connectivity. Check the routes, the relevant filters, and the response from the destination.

questions.title: Security Groups and Network ACLs
questions.prompt: An AWS designer selects rules that allow requests and their responses in a VPC. Choose two statements that correctly describe how Security Groups and Network ACLs work.

choices.text: A Security Group is stateful and allows responses to permitted traffic based on connection state.
choices.explanation: You do not need to add a reverse-direction rule for responses to permitted traffic.

choices.text: A Network ACL is applied at the instance level and tracks connection state.
choices.explanation: A Network ACL is applied at the subnet level and does not track connection state.

choices.text: A Network ACL permits inbound and outbound traffic separately.
choices.explanation: A Network ACL evaluates rules separately for each traffic direction.

choices.text: A Network ACL is not evaluated if a route exists.
choices.explanation: Even when a route determines the destination, whether traffic is allowed is evaluated separately by the Network ACL.

learning.concept: Filters that track connection state and filters that do not
learning.reason: Security Groups track connection state. Network ACLs match rules separately for each direction.

questions.title: Network ACLs and Return Traffic
questions.prompt: A network administrator controls an HTTPS connection between an Application Load Balancer and EC2 in different subnets using Network ACLs. Choose two incorrect statements about the configuration decision.

choices.text: Check Network ACL rules in both directions in the subnet containing the ALB and the subnet containing EC2.
choices.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless.

choices.text: If the Security Group is stateful, outbound rules in the Network ACL are unnecessary.
choices.explanation: Correct. Network ACLs independently evaluate outbound traffic as well.

choices.text: Consider the return ephemeral ports.
choices.explanation: This is required when designing Network ACLs.

choices.text: Because Network ACLs apply only to EC2, do not inspect the subnet containing the ALB.
choices.explanation: Correct. Network ACLs apply to subnets.

learning.concept: Allowing traffic across subnet boundaries
learning.reason: Allow the required ports in both directions for requests and responses in each subnet containing the ALB and EC2.

questions.title: VPC Troubleshooting Order
questions.prompt: An operations engineer confirmed that the order API in the VPC resolves to the intended IP and that the application on EC2 is listening on port 443. The application still cannot be reached from another subnet. Choose one correct next check.

choices.text: Open all Security Group access and then create a route.
choices.explanation: Diagnose by examining the path and each filter without removing controls.

choices.text: Check the route, the Network ACL at the subnet boundary, and the Security Groups applied to the network interface.
choices.explanation: Investigate the path and the two traffic controls separately.

choices.text: Delete the Network ACL and then check the destination.
choices.explanation: Diagnose without destroying evidence through changes.

learning.concept: Investigating the connection path after confirming the destination
learning.reason: Examine the route between the target subnets, the Network ACL, and the resource’s Security Group.

questions.title: Reachability to an Interface VPC Endpoint
questions.prompt: An operations engineer is investigating why AWS services cannot be accessed through an interface VPC endpoint. The service name resolves to the endpoint's private IP address. Select one investigation approach that is incorrect.

choices.text: Verify that resolving the service name returns the private IP address of the VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: To use the intended endpoint, the name must resolve to that endpoint's address.

choices.text: Because name resolution succeeded, skip checking the route, the source's outbound rules, and the endpoint's security group.
choices.explanation: Even if name resolution succeeds, problems may remain with the route or communication permissions.

choices.text: If a VPC endpoint policy applies, verify that the caller, operation, and target resource are permitted.
choices.explanation: Even when communication is possible, the endpoint policy may deny a required operation.

learning.concept: Interface VPC endpoint reachability
learning.reason: Even after verifying name resolution, a route from the source to the endpoint and permissions at both ends are required.

questions.title: Checks After Peering
questions.prompt: A designer has approved peering between two VPCs that use nonoverlapping CIDRs and wants to call an internal API in one VPC from an EC2 instance in the other. Select two settings that must be checked before communication.

choices.text: Place a route to the peer CIDR in the route tables of both VPCs.
choices.explanation: Correct. Creating a VPC peering connection does not automatically add routes to each subnet's route table.

choices.text: The security groups and network ACLs are automatically opened to all traffic.
choices.explanation: Permission settings are not changed automatically.

choices.text: Verify the required security group and network ACL permissions on both sides.
choices.explanation: Correct.

choices.text: A return route is unnecessary.
choices.explanation: Bidirectional communication requires a return path.

learning.concept: Routes and permissions required for VPC peering
learning.reason: After approving the connection, place routes to the peer in both VPCs and allow the required inbound and outbound traffic.

questions.title: Troubleshooting Cross-VPC Connectivity
questions.prompt: A client cannot connect to an internal API in another VPC. The operations engineer has confirmed that the API name returns the correct private IP address and that the source subnet's route is correct. During the investigation, communication must remain limited to the required peer and port. Under these conditions, select two incorrect actions.

choices.text: Check the security groups, network ACLs, and return path for the source and destination.
choices.explanation: Even after confirming the source route, the cause may remain in rules that permit communication or in the path for responses to return.

choices.text: Because the API name resolves correctly, skip checking the rules that permit communication.
choices.explanation: Resolving the name does not guarantee that a connection can be made on the target port.

choices.text: If a VPC endpoint policy applies, verify that the caller, operation, and target resource are permitted.
choices.explanation: If the policy denies a required operation, the call fails even when the route to the destination and communication permissions are correct.

choices.text: Until the investigation is complete, open communication from all security groups to all addresses.
choices.explanation: Even a temporary change violates the condition that communication be limited to the required peer and port.

learning.concept: Narrowing the investigation when the route is correct
learning.reason: Identify the communication direction and required port, then check the return route and filters to find the cause without broadly expanding permissions.

units.title: CI/CD Workflow
units.summary: Learn the workflow of checking changes in small increments and gradually delivering validated artifacts to production.
units.objective: Explain the process for checking changes and why the same artifacts are distributed to each environment.
explanation: In continuous integration, changes are integrated frequently, and builds and tests help identify problems early.
When promoting changes to a new environment, compare the identifier of the validated artifact with the inspection results.
units.example: Check changes to the Order API and distribute the same container image to the validation environment and production.

learningObjectives.text: Explain the purpose of integrating changes frequently and checking them with builds and tests.
Distinguish between the process of making validated changes ready for release and the process of automating their deployment to production.
Explain why the same artifacts are used across environments and why the item being validated must be identifiable.
Decide whether to proceed to the next stage based on the inspection results and operational conditions.

sections.title: Integrate Small Changes and Test Them Immediately
paragraphs: Continuous integration (CI) is a method in which developers frequently integrate changes into a shared branch and run a build and tests each time. When the scope of a change is small, it is easier to connect a failed check with the change that caused it.
A build creates, for example, executables or container images for distribution from source code. Testing examines whether the change works as specified.

With AWS CodePipeline, processes such as source retrieval, building, testing, approval, and distribution can be connected as a pipeline. The conditions for proceeding to each stage are determined by the team's requirements.

example.scenario: Immediately after a development team integrated a change to the order API, the API integration test failed.
steps: Check the failed test's name, input, expected value, and actual response.
Identify the change that first caused the test to fail, and reproduce the cause with a small change.
Apply a fix, rerun the same check, and confirm that the expected result is obtained.
example.outcome: The team identified and fixed the broken processing before moving the change to production.

misconception.claim: The executable was created by the build, so the order processing should work correctly too.
misconception.correction: A successful build shows that a distributable artifact was created. Testing is needed to verify that order processing works as specified.

takeaways: Repeat change integration and testing in small increments.
Builds and tests have different roles.

sections.title: Distinguish Continuous Delivery from Continuous Deployment
paragraphs: In continuous delivery, changes are built and tested so that they remain ready to be released to production at any time. When to release them is determined by approvals or business rules.

In continuous deployment, changes that pass all required checks are released to production without human approval. Automatic monitoring, along with stopping or rolling back when an anomaly is detected, is designed as part of the process.

example.scenario: Billing changes are normally approved by an operations staff member during business hours, while changes to static help are automatically released to production when the checks succeed.
steps: Confirm the time periods during which changes can be made and the conditions for proceeding to production.
Add an approval stage for changes that require approval, and incorporate the necessary checks for both types of change.
example.outcome: This allows the process that verifies the content and the decision to release it to production to be operated separately.

misconception.claim: If there is a stage where an operations staff member approves the change, automated tests can be omitted.
misconception.correction: Automated tests examine whether the change works as specified. Approval confirms conditions for proceeding to production, such as the impact scope and application time.

takeaways: Distinguish the process that makes a release-ready state from the process that actually releases to production.
Define the conditions for proceeding to production according to the type of change.

sections.title: Deliver Validated Artifacts to Production Unchanged
paragraphs: Files for distribution and container images created by a build are called artifacts. Rebuilding separately for each environment can change the dependencies used or the files generated, causing the contents to differ from those validated.

Identify artifacts by a build number or digest, and use the same artifacts in the validation environment and production. Environment-specific values such as endpoints are specified in the deployment destination's configuration.

example.scenario: The order API's container image was tested in the validation environment. Confirm the candidate for production distribution.
steps: Compare the digest from the build result with the digest used in the validation environment.
Specify the same digest in the production deployment configuration, and pass the endpoint from the production configuration.
Record the digest running after distribution and the monitoring results.
example.outcome: You can confirm that what passed the checks matches what runs in production.

misconception.claim: If the same source is used, separate builds for validation and production will produce the same thing.
misconception.correction: Artifacts can change because of dependencies and build-time configuration. Use the identifier of the validated artifact to distribute that same artifact.

takeaways: Specify artifacts with information that identifies their contents.
Treat values that depend on the runtime environment as configuration for that environment.

source.label: AWS CodePipeline input and output artifacts

sections.title: Define Conditions for Proceeding to the Next Stage
paragraphs: A quality gate is a condition used to decide, based on validation results, whether to proceed to the next stage. Before making a change, define the values used for the decision and the passing criteria, such as successful required tests, processing time, and error rate.

Even when beginning a rollout with a small number of users, expand the release scope only after obtaining results that meet the conditions. If the conditions are not met, stop the rollout, record the results, and investigate the cause.

example.scenario: A new version of the order API is being rolled out to part of the audience. The team has decided not to expand the release if the order error rate exceeds 1%.
steps: Check the requests targeted by the new version and the number of errors.
Because the error rate was 2%, stop the rollout.
Record the measurement results and the identifier of the deployed artifact, and isolate the cause.
example.outcome: Based on the conditions and evidence, the team prevented the problem's impact from spreading.

misconception.claim: The tests were all run, so it is acceptable to proceed to the next stage even if some failed.
misconception.correction: In addition to running the tests, the defined passing criteria must be met. If the conditions are not met, investigate the cause before proceeding with the release.

takeaways: Define the passing criteria and the action to take on failure in advance.
Record the results and the artifact identifier.

questions.title: The Role of CI
questions.prompt: The development team wants to inspect changes quickly immediately after receiving a commit for the order API. Choose one correct description of continuous integration (CI).

choices.text: Incorporate commits and automatically run builds and tests to inspect changes quickly.
choices.explanation: CI uses commits as the starting point for builds and tests, detecting failures at an early stage.

choices.text: Once CI succeeds, production safety is guaranteed unconditionally.
choices.explanation: CI success means that the specified checks succeeded; it does not guarantee against all production risks.

choices.text: Check only whether the build succeeds, and run tests after deployment to production.
choices.explanation: CI requires running builds and tests so that failures are not passed to later stages.

learning.reason: CI is a mechanism for integrating changes in small increments and inspecting them quickly through builds and tests.
learning.concept: Purpose of continuous integration

questions.title: Tracing the Cause of Integration Failures
questions.prompt: The development team that changed the order API wants to narrow down the cause of a failure during integration. Choose one incorrect approach.

choices.text: Run the same build and tests for each small commit.
choices.explanation: The shorter the distance between a change and its test results, the easier it is to trace the cause.

choices.text: When a failure occurs, check the logs, inputs, and changes, then rerun the same checks after making a fix.
choices.explanation: This is the correct approach: do not pass the failure to later stages, and verify it under the same conditions.

choices.text: Do not retain failure logs; combine several weeks of changes and then inspect them manually.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. The differences become larger and the basis for the fix is lost, making it impossible to narrow down the cause.

learning.reason: By checking small changes with the same tests and retaining evidence of failures, you can trace the cause.
learning.concept: CI operations with small changes

questions.title: Using CI Results
questions.prompt: The release manager uses the CI results for the order API to decide whether to deploy it to the next environment. Choose two appropriate actions.

choices.text: Because CI succeeded, deploy to production without checking the monitoring plan or the next quality gate.
choices.explanation: CI success alone does not guarantee production safety; the next deployment conditions must be evaluated.

choices.text: Evaluate the next quality gate and deployment conditions for the candidate that passed the defined checks.
choices.explanation: CI results are test evidence used for downstream decisions.

choices.text: Discard the test results and manually rebuild from the same source for production.
choices.explanation: This breaks the correspondence with the test results and could change the artifact being deployed.

choices.text: Do not allow failed checks to proceed downstream; review the logs and changes, fix the issue, and rerun the checks.
choices.explanation: This stops failures early and verifies the fix using the same checks.

learning.reason: Pass CI results downstream as evidence for the next quality gate, and verify failures after fixing them by running the same checks again.
learning.concept: CI Results and Downstream Decisions

questions.title: delivery and deployment
questions.prompt: The release engineer chooses how to deploy the order API from the test environment to production. Choose two incorrect statements about continuous delivery and continuous deployment.

choices.text: Continuous delivery keeps tested changes in a state where they can be released at any time.
choices.explanation: This is the correct description of delivery.

choices.text: Continuous delivery is a method that always deploys automatically to production without human approval.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Automatic deployment to production without human approval is continuous deployment.

choices.text: Continuous deployment is a method that automatically deploys changes that have passed the defined quality gates all the way to production.
choices.explanation: This is the correct description of deployment.

choices.text: Manual approval is not a substitute for testing; it can serve as a decision point for reviewing impact and monitoring.
choices.explanation: This correctly describes the role of approval in the prompt.

choices.text: If manual approval is added, builds and tests do not need to be run.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Approval is not a substitute for automated checks.

learning.reason: Delivery means keeping changes releasable, deployment means automatically deploying them through to production, and approval is a decision point separate from testing.
learning.concept: Distinguishing delivery, deployment, and approval

questions.title: Pre-Production Approval
questions.prompt: The release manager deploys a tested web application from the test environment to production. Choose one appropriate use of manual approval.

choices.text: Make automated tests unnecessary and proceed based only on the approver’s impression.
choices.explanation: Manual approval is not a substitute for automated tests.

choices.text: Review the change impact, change window, and monitoring plan before deciding whether to proceed.
choices.explanation: Manual approval can be used as a responsible decision point before deployment.

choices.text: Rebuild a production-specific artifact after approval.
choices.explanation: This is not the purpose of approval because it creates a difference from the tested artifact.

learning.reason: At approval time, review the impact, change window, and monitoring plan, and decide whether to proceed separately from testing.
learning.concept: The Role of Manual Approval

questions.title: Choosing a deployment method
questions.prompt: The payments team automatically deploys tested artifacts all the way to production without human approval. Select two correct actions according to the passage.

choices.text: This method is continuous deployment, which automatically deploys changes that have passed the defined quality gates.
choices.explanation: A method that automatically deploys to production without human approval is continuous deployment.

choices.text: Because it is continuous delivery, it is always automatically deployed to production without human approval.
choices.explanation: Delivery means that the release is in a releasable state; it does not necessarily mean automatic deployment to production.

choices.text: Because automatic deployment was selected, proceed to the next stage without recording quality-gate failures.
choices.explanation: Even with automatic deployment, the next stage must be stopped when the quality gate is not met.

choices.text: Verify by identifier that the artifact deployed to production is the same as the artifact tested in the validation environment.
choices.explanation: Regardless of the deployment method, the tested artifact and the deployed artifact can be traced.

choices.text: Rebuild a production artifact for each environmental difference, then deploy it automatically.
choices.explanation: Rebuilding creates a difference from the tested artifact.

learning.reason: Even with continuous deployment, maintain the quality gates and artifact traceability while deploying automatically.
learning.concept: Automatic deployment and testing traceability

questions.title: How to track artifacts
questions.prompt: A release manager deploys to production a container image verified in the validation environment. Select one incorrect statement about artifacts.

choices.text: An artifact is a deployable unit, such as a package or container image generated by a build.
choices.explanation: This is the correct definition of an artifact described in the passage.

choices.text: Identifying an artifact by its digest or version makes it possible to track the deployed artifact.
choices.explanation: A version or digest is a correct identifier for specifying an artifact.

choices.text: Even if artifacts are rebuilt for each environment, the tested artifact and the deployed artifact are always identical as long as the source commit is the same.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Rebuilding can cause the artifact tested and the artifact deployed to production to differ.

learning.reason: Fixing an artifact by its identifier makes it possible to track the tested artifact and the deployed artifact.
learning.concept: Artifacts and identifiers

questions.title: Tracking production artifacts
questions.prompt: An auditor verifies the correspondence between the artifacts deployed to production and the tests. Select two incorrect actions.

choices.text: Use only the release manager’s memory as the evidence linking the artifacts to the tests.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. It is not reproducible evidence.

choices.text: Save the source commit, the artifact version or digest, and the test results.
choices.explanation: This is the correct action for associating the change, deployed artifact, and test results.

choices.text: Use the digest tested in the validation environment for the production deployment as well.
choices.explanation: This is the correct action for keeping the tested artifact and the deployed artifact identical.

choices.text: Record a production artifact rebuilt for production as if it were the same as the tested artifact.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. The rebuilt artifact may differ from the tested artifact.

choices.text: Provide environment-specific endpoints as external configuration and do not change the artifact itself.
choices.explanation: This is the correct action for handling environmental differences while maintaining the same artifact.

learning.reason: Store the commit, digest, and test results, then promote the same artifact to enable tracking.
learning.concept: Artifact traceability

questions.title: Environment Differences and Promotion
questions.prompt: You are deploying a web service whose destination URL differs between the test and production environments to the next environment without changing the same artifact. Select two correct actions.

choices.text: Embed the URL for each environment and rebuild the production artifact.
choices.explanation: Rebuilding creates a difference from the tested artifact.

choices.text: Provide the destination URL as external configuration and deploy the digest tested in the test environment to the next environment.
choices.explanation: This handles environment differences without rebuilding the artifact and keeps the tested and deployed targets identical.

choices.text: Have an operator manually change the production destination each time without keeping a record.
choices.explanation: This loses reproducibility and auditability.

choices.text: Using the “latest” tag means that the tested artifact does not need to be identified.
choices.explanation: The “latest” tag alone cannot fix the exact artifact being deployed.

choices.text: Associate and store the source commit, artifact digest, and test results.
choices.explanation: This is the correct action because it enables tracking of the change, artifact, and tests.

learning.reason: Separate environment differences into external configuration, promote the same digest, and preserve the test evidence.
learning.concept: Immutable artifacts and promotion

questions.title: Quality Gate Stop Conditions
questions.prompt: The release operator decides whether to deploy to production based on the results from the test environment. Select one correct description of a quality gate.

choices.text: It is a stop point that allows progression to the next stage solely because the test was executed, regardless of the result.
choices.explanation: A quality gate evaluates whether the result meets defined conditions, not merely whether the test was executed.

choices.text: It is a stop point that prevents artifacts that do not meet the defined tests and passing criteria from being deployed to the next environment.
choices.explanation: This is the correct role of a quality gate.

choices.text: It is a mechanism that lowers the threshold on the spot when requirements are not met in order to keep the scheduled time.
choices.explanation: Lowering conditions without justification when requirements are not met defeats the purpose of a quality gate.

learning.reason: A quality gate is a stop point that prevents artifacts failing to meet defined conditions from progressing to later stages.
learning.concept: Quality gate definition

questions.title: When the Test Environment Fails to Meet the Passing Criteria
questions.prompt: A required test failed in the test environment, and the error rate also exceeded the quality gate threshold. Select the one action that is incorrect for the release owner.

choices.text: Prioritize the scheduled time, deploy to production, and investigate the cause afterward.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. When the quality gate is not met, stop deployment to the next environment without spreading the impact.

choices.text: Stop deployment to the next environment, maintain the known-good version, and investigate the cause of the failure.
choices.explanation: When the criteria are not met, do not proceed to later stages; preserve the known-good version and the test evidence.

choices.text: Keep the defined conditions unchanged and rerun the same tests after making the correction.
choices.explanation: The correct response is to fix the cause and then verify it under the same quality gate conditions.

learning.reason: When the test environment fails to meet the quality gate, stop promotion, maintain the known-good version, resolve the cause, and then retest.
learning.concept: Response when the quality gate is not met

questions.title: Operating a gradual rollout
questions.prompt: Operations staff deploy new build artifacts to part of production and expand the release scope while using the same tested artifacts to limit the impact. Select two incorrect approaches to this deployment method.

choices.text: Distribute the same tested artifacts to part of production and expand the release scope only when predefined criteria are met.
choices.explanation: Using the same artifacts preserves consistency with the validation. Limiting the release scope makes it less likely that an incident will spread.

choices.text: To release as scheduled, raise the upper limit for the acceptable error rate after the criteria have been exceeded.
choices.explanation: Loosening the stop conditions defined before release to match results during operation cannot sufficiently limit the impact on users.

choices.text: Record the acceptance criteria, the responsible person when a failure occurs, the log storage location, and the rerun procedure in advance.
choices.explanation: The decisions to stop and rerun can follow the same procedure even when the responsible person changes.

choices.text: Delete the failed test logs and the artifacts from the successfully running release before redistributing them.
choices.explanation: This loses the records needed to investigate the cause and the artifacts that could be used for rollback.

choices.text: If the criteria are not met, stop expanding the release scope, fix the cause, and then test again under the same conditions.
choices.explanation: The results can be checked against the same criteria, allowing a decision on whether to proceed again.

learning.concept: Gradual release and artifact consistency
learning.reason: Start with a small release scope and apply monitoring and stop conditions. Use the same tested artifacts for the next stage as well.

units.title: Testing and quality gates
units.summary: Learn how to choose among unit, integration, and E2E tests and verify results under the same conditions.
units.objective: Define the scope and reproduction conditions for tests, and use the inspection results to make release decisions and prevent defects from recurring.
explanation: First choose the scope to investigate based on where a defect is likely to be.
Record the inputs and expected values used in the tests so that you can verify before and after the fix using the same procedure.
units.example: Verify the order tax calculation and the flow that saves an order from the order API to the database using tests with different scopes.

learningObjectives.text: Distinguish the scope and role of unit, integration, and E2E tests.
Specify the conditions and expected values that affect the outcome so that the test results can be reproduced.
Define the checks and pass criteria required to move the change to the next stage.
Collect evidence of the failure so that the same defect can be detected after the fix.

sections.title: Choose the scope to verify with testing.
paragraphs: In unit tests, for example, you check the inputs and return value of a function that calculates tax. Because the processing scope is small, it is easier to narrow down the cause of a failure.
Integration tests examine the boundaries where multiple components are connected. For example, they verify whether an order API can connect to the database and correctly save the required columns.

In end-to-end (E2E) tests, you verify the flow from an entry point close to the user through login, order entry, and order confirmation. Because the flow crosses multiple functions, these tests can find important defects, but you narrow down the cause by examining each process.

example.scenario: We changed the order screen and the tax-calculation code. We will check the tax amount, the order record, and the operation flow.
steps: With fixed inputs, inspect the return value of the function that calculates the tax amount.
Verify writing to and reading from the database through the order API.
Place an order from the user interface and verify that order completion is displayed.
example.outcome: When a defect occurs, you can narrow down whether it happened in the calculation, data integration, or the user’s operation.

misconception.claim: Because the order completed once, you can conclude that the boundary values for the tax calculation are also correct.
misconception.correction: The operations and input range that passed are limited. Verify tax boundary values with unit tests, where inputs can be rearranged easily.

takeaways: Separate the test scope into calculation rules, integration, and user operations.
Verify first within a scope where failures are easy to find.

sections.title: Set the inputs, prerequisites, and expected values so the test can be reproduced.
paragraphs: To reproduce a test, clarify what to input, from what state to run it, and what should be returned. If the result changes because of the date and time or an external response, also record the values and conditions used.

In unit tests, fixing the time and external responses lets you verify a specific rule with a small number of inputs. When examining an actual database connection, prepare a test environment that can connect and separate the data used by the tests.

example.scenario: We are testing order processing in which the tax rate changes at midnight. The specification says that the result changes according to the time on the day of execution.
steps: Fix the date and time, time zone, and expected tax-inclusive amount.
Prepare inputs corresponding to just before and just after the tax rate changes.
Even when the same test is run at different times, verify that it produces the same result for each fixed set of conditions.
example.outcome: Another person in charge can investigate the failed input under the same conditions.

misconception.claim: Even if the inputs are different each time, rerunning a test that fails occasionally is sufficient.
misconception.correction: If the inputs or execution conditions differ, you cannot confirm the same phenomenon. Record the conditions at the time of failure and fix the inputs needed for reproduction.

takeaways: State the expected results and variable factors explicitly.
When multiple tests modify the same data, keep the conditions from becoming mixed.

sections.title: Use test results as the conditions for proceeding
paragraphs: Quality gates define what is tested, the pass criteria, and how to proceed to the next stage. For example, they prevent a production deployment from starting when an E2E test that verifies login and ordering fails.
AWS CodeBuild test reports show which tests succeeded or failed. Recording execution results makes it easier to investigate which change introduced a defect.

example.scenario: For changes to the order API, unit tests, integration tests, and E2E tests that confirm order completion are all required.
steps: Check the results of all required tests.
Stop the deployment because the E2E test that confirms order completion failed.
After reproducing and fixing the failure, make the artifact that passed the same tests a candidate again.
example.outcome: This prevents changes that affect users from proceeding to production while failures remain.

misconception.claim: If test execution records exist, the quality gate can be passed even if some tests fail.
misconception.correction: Execution records are evidence for making a decision. Confirm which tests were required and which criteria were met.

takeaways: Make decisions based on test results and pass criteria.
Record the tested artifact together with its results.

sections.title: Reproduce failures so the same defect can be detected
paragraphs: When a test fails, first record where the actual result differed from the expected result, the input, the changes executed, and the logs. Isolate the possible cause one by one, such as the code, test data, or environment.

After fixing the cause, retain a regression test that can reproduce the failed conditions. Confirming that it fails before the fix and succeeds after the fix makes it possible to detect when the same defect returns.

example.scenario: When the order time was close to the time when the tax rate changed, a defect caused the billing amount to shift because the effective date was off by one day. A quality specialist reproduces the defect.
steps: Fix the time and time zone of the failed order.
Exclude other processing and find the smallest input that causes the same discrepancy.
Verify the post-fix result with that input and add it to the regression tests.
example.outcome: This makes it possible to detect when a defect under the same conditions returns in a later change.

misconception.claim: There is no reason to retain the input or tests from the failure because the fix has been completed.
misconception.correction: If you retain the input and expected result and incorporate them into a test, you can find the same defect even if it occurs in a later change.

takeaways: Retain the information needed for reproduction.
Run regression tests using the smallest conditions that caused the failure.

questions.title: Define test granularity
questions.prompt: A developer uses unit, integration, and E2E tests appropriately to verify the quality of an order API. Select one correct explanation.

choices.text: Unit tests verify local rules, integration tests verify service boundaries, and E2E tests verify user journeys.
choices.explanation: This is the correct explanation corresponding to the scopes distinguished in the prompt.

choices.text: Integration tests verify only users’ screen interactions.
choices.explanation: A sequence of user journeys from the screen is the scope of E2E tests, while integration tests verify boundaries such as APIs and databases.

choices.text: If unit tests pass, authentication and data formats between services have also been verified.
choices.explanation: Unit tests alone cannot verify actual service boundaries.

learning.reason: Separating the scope for each type of test makes it possible to explain the failures detected.
learning.concept: Roles of unit, integration, and E2E tests

questions.title: Diagnosing E2E Failures
questions.prompt: A developer narrows down the cause of a failed E2E test for completed purchases. Select one incorrect response.

choices.text: Verify the discount-calculation rules with unit tests.
choices.explanation: Checking local rules within a small scope makes it easier to narrow down the cause.

choices.text: Delete the integration test with the payment API to investigate the cause faster.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Removing service-boundary checks prevents problems occurring in the payment integration from being detected.

choices.text: Verify the data formats of the order API and payment API with an integration test.
choices.explanation: This allows failures at the service boundary to be investigated separately from the E2E test.

learning.reason: By testing E2E failures separately as local rules and service-boundary issues, their causes can be isolated efficiently.
learning.concept: Diagnosing failures by test granularity

questions.title: Order-Path Test Design
questions.prompt: Before release, the order-service development team verifies the discount-calculation rules and that users can log in and complete a purchase. Select two tests appropriate for these respective checks.

choices.text: Unit-test the discount-calculation rules with fixed inputs.
choices.explanation: Local rules can be checked quickly with unit tests.

choices.text: Verify the discount-calculation rules only by checking whether an order can be placed from the screen.
choices.explanation: Even if one purchase path succeeds, you cannot conclude that all discount conditions and boundary values are correct.

choices.text: Delete the E2E test from login through purchase completion and replace it with unit tests only.
choices.explanation: Unit tests alone cannot verify the user journey.

choices.text: Run an E2E test from login through purchase completion.
choices.explanation: This verifies an important path close to the user experience.

choices.text: Investigate every failure only by rerunning the E2E test.
choices.explanation: An E2E test with a broad cause range alone makes it harder to narrow down mismatches in local rules or service boundaries.

learning.reason: Verify expected values for the discount rules for each input, and verify the purchase through the same sequence of actions as a user.
learning.concept: Multi-granularity test design

questions.title: Reproducible Tests
questions.prompt: A test engineer designs tests so that order calculations can be verified under the same conditions even after changes. Select two incorrect items.

choices.text: Explicitly specify the inputs, prerequisites, expected values, and execution conditions.
choices.explanation: This is a correct design required to rerun the test under the same conditions.

choices.text: Fix or record variations in time, random numbers, and external responses.
choices.explanation: Controlling or recording factors that change the result is correct test design.

choices.text: Determine the expected value from the actual result each time the test runs.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Creating the expected value from the actual result risks treating a defect as the correct result.

choices.text: Delete failed inputs and actual results to speed up the investigation.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Inputs and actual results from failures should be saved as evidence for reproduction and root-cause investigation.

choices.text: Test boundary values and abnormal responses as separate cases.
choices.explanation: This is a correct design that explicitly verifies specification branches.

learning.reason: By deciding the inputs, expected values, and execution conditions in advance and preserving failure evidence, the same test can be rerun.
learning.concept: Conditions for test reproducibility

questions.title: Testing a Tax Rate Change
questions.prompt: A developer is validating order calculations that include the date and time when the tax rate changes. Choose one correct way to make the test reproducible.

choices.text: Save the tax-inclusive amount after execution as the expected value for the next run.
choices.explanation: If the expected value is created from the actual result, calculation defects cannot be detected.

choices.text: Fix the effective date and time, tax rate, tax-exclusive amount, and expected tax-inclusive amount from the specification.
choices.explanation: Fixing the time-dependent inputs and expected value in advance allows the test to be rerun under the same conditions.

choices.text: Combine the boundary-date-and-time case with the normal-value cases and check only one case.
choices.explanation: The boundary where the tax rate changes must be checked as a separate case.

choices.text: Do not record the input and actual result when a failure occurs; update only the time and rerun the test.
choices.explanation: This loses the evidence needed to reproduce the conditions and investigate the cause.

learning.reason: By fixing the variable date and time and tax rate, and defining the expected value from the specification, the result can be compared.
learning.concept: Fixed inputs and expected values

questions.title: Rerunning Tests Across an External Boundary
questions.prompt: A test engineer is investigating intermittent failures in an integration test connecting an order service and a delivery API. Choose two correct approaches for reproducible investigation and validation.

choices.text: Isolate the test data and save the input, actual result, commit, and test environment when a failure occurs.
choices.explanation: This prevents contamination from other runs and allows the same failure conditions to be investigated.

choices.text: Replace the delivery API’s actual authentication and data format with unit-test mocks only.
choices.explanation: This cannot verify the actual service boundary, which is the purpose of an integration test.

choices.text: Every time the test fails, adjust the expected value to match the delivery API’s actual response.
choices.explanation: Matching the expected value to the actual result prevents contract violations from being detected.

choices.text: Use shared test data as is and omit cleanup after a failure.
choices.explanation: Other runs may change the data, causing accidental passes or failures.

choices.text: Design setup, execution, and cleanup, and compare the expected value at the actual boundary.
choices.explanation: This keeps the test environment and evidence reusable while validating the actual boundary.

learning.reason: Combining an actual service boundary, isolated data, and failure evidence makes it possible to rerun the integration test.
learning.concept: Test design including an external boundary

questions.title: Defining quality gates
questions.prompt: The release manager decides whether to deploy to production based on the results from the validation environment. Select one incorrect statement about quality gates.

choices.text: Do not deploy changes that fail to meet the required tests and passing criteria to the next environment.
choices.explanation: This is the correct role of a quality gate.

choices.text: Allow the quality gate to pass based solely on the fact that the tests were run, regardless of the results.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. The decision is based on the results and thresholds of the required tests, not on whether they were run.

choices.text: A quality gate should include the stopping condition for failures and the location where the audit trail is stored.
choices.explanation: This is the correct design for reproducing stoppage and investigation.

learning.reason: A quality gate is a condition that stops progression to later stages based on results and thresholds.
learning.concept: Quality-gate passing conditions

questions.title: Operating CodeBuild Reports
questions.prompt: A release manager detected a required integration test failure and insufficient coverage in CodeBuild. Select two actions that are incorrect before deploying to production.

choices.text: Fail the quality gate, stop deployment to the next environment, and save the CodeBuild report.
choices.explanation: When required checks fail and thresholds are not met, the correct response is to stop subsequent stages and preserve the evidence.

choices.text: Lower the coverage threshold only this time to meet the release schedule.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Lowering the standard to match the result defeats the purpose of the quality gate.

choices.text: Inspect the test reports specified under reports in the CodeBuild buildspec file, and confirm the target commit and execution environment.
choices.explanation: Associating the reports with the execution conditions makes it possible to investigate failure rates and cause trends.

choices.text: Delete the failed report and use only a rerun as evidence of success.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Deleting the failure report removes the basis for investigating the cause and validating the rerun.

choices.text: After fixing the cause, rerun the tests under the same required conditions.
choices.explanation: Maintaining the defined conditions makes the decision reproducible.

learning.reason: Use CodeBuild reports as evidence, stop when thresholds are not met, and rerun the checks under the same conditions.
learning.concept: Report-based quality-gate operation

questions.title: Evidence for Promotion Decisions
questions.prompt: The release owner uses the results of multiple CodeBuild runs to decide whether to deploy the artifacts to the next environment. Select two correct practices.

choices.text: Document the required tests, coverage thresholds, and stopping conditions as quality gates.
choices.explanation: You can decide in advance what to measure and which results should stop the process.

choices.text: Store each build's test report with links to the commit and execution environment.
choices.explanation: Associating the results with the changes and environment makes it possible to investigate failure rates and trends.

choices.text: Use only the memory of the person who viewed the screen as evidence that the gate was passed.
choices.explanation: Without stored reports, the decision and investigation cannot be reproduced.

choices.text: For builds with a high failure rate, lower the threshold without checking the cause.
choices.explanation: Instead of adjusting the criteria to the results, investigate the cause and maintain the conditions.

choices.text: Delete failed required tests and make the decision based only on the remaining successes.
choices.explanation: Deleting required tests hides failures that the quality gates are supposed to detect.

learning.reason: Linking quality-gate conditions and CodeBuild reports to the changes and environment makes promotion decisions and failure investigations reproducible.
learning.concept: Evidence for Quality Gates

questions.title: Purpose of Regression Tests
questions.prompt: A developer fixed a defect that produced an incorrect billing amount for a particular input. Select one purpose of retaining the smallest failing input and expected value as a regression test.

choices.text: Save no failure log and simply rerun all tests so that the cause can be determined.
choices.explanation: Without logs or reproduction conditions, it becomes harder to narrow down the cause.

choices.text: Ensure that even if the same input defect recurs, it can be detected using only manual memory.
choices.explanation: Recurrence detection cannot be left to human memory.

choices.text: Add the input and expected value that confirmed the fix to the CI required tests, and automatically detect recurrence under the same conditions.
choices.explanation: Adding the input that reproduced the failure to checks run for every change makes it possible to find the defect if it returns.

learning.reason: Retaining the smallest case corresponding to the fixed cause makes it possible to detect recurrence in the future.
learning.concept: Role of regression tests

questions.title: Handling Failure Evidence
questions.prompt: A developer confirmed a test failure in the order API during CI. As the first response to investigate the cause, select one incorrect action.

choices.text: Record the first mismatch, inputs, actual results, logs, and the change commit.
choices.explanation: This is the correct starting point for reproducing the same failure and narrowing down the layer causing it.

choices.text: Reduce it to the smallest failing case and investigate the layer where the expected and actual results first diverge.
choices.explanation: This is the correct response for isolating the cause without expanding the scope of the change.

choices.text: After fixing the cause, add the same conditions to a regression test.
choices.explanation: This is the correct response for ensuring that the same defect can be detected by future quality gates.

choices.text: Without confirming the cause, delete the failed test so that the pipeline passes.
choices.explanation: This is incorrect. Deleting the test hides the defect and prevents its recurrence from being detected.

learning.reason: Preserve evidence that reproduces the failure and convert it into a regression test addressing the cause.
learning.concept: From failure investigation to regression prevention

questions.title: Managing IT/E2E Side Effects
questions.prompt: A quality engineer runs integration tests and E2E tests in parallel that write to the same database, designing them so that individual tests can be reproduced when they fail. Select two incorrect actions for this requirement.

choices.text: Separate the test environments and, even when sharing an external database, use different records for each test.
choices.explanation: Even if the test environments are separated, tests can modify the same rows when they use the same external database. Separating the data used by each test prevents interference.

choices.text: Share the same delivery-address record across all tests and rely on the execution order.
choices.explanation: This harms reproducibility. When different tests modify the same data, accidental passes or failures can occur.

choices.text: Skip cleanup after a failure and leave intermediate data for the next run.
choices.explanation: This harms reproducibility. The remaining data changes the conditions of the next run.

choices.text: Include setup, execution, cleanup, and result reporting in the test procedure.
choices.explanation: This is the correct design for rerunning the same conditions and preserving evidence of the results.

choices.text: Save the inputs, test environment, and logs from failures and use them to investigate the cause.
choices.explanation: This is the correct response for preserving the reproduction conditions and using them in the next investigation and regression tests.

source.label: Running parallel tests in AWS CodeBuild

learning.reason: When isolation, cleanup, and evidence are made part of one sequence of steps, reproducibility can be maintained while verifying the actual boundaries.
learning.concept: IT/E2E data isolation and side-effect management

units.title: Deployment and Recovery
units.summary: Learn how to safely update an order API, from deciding the scope of the release to recovering after a failure.
units.objective: Choose a deployment method that limits the impact of changes and determine how to recover the application and data when something goes wrong.
explanation: For a safe update, you must decide in advance which users to switch over, under what circumstances to stop, and how far you can roll back.
units.example: Consider how to decide to stop the release and recover when some requests are sent to the updated version and the order success rate decreases.

learningObjectives.text: Compare the impact on users and the required infrastructure, and choose an update method.
Measure the impact on users and determine whether to continue or stop the release.
Compare the time required for recovery and data compatibility, and explain the procedure to follow.
Application rollback and database recovery can be planned separately.

sections.title: Choose the deployment scope and switching strategy
paragraphs: A rolling update gradually replaces running tasks with new tasks while keeping the service running. Because old and new tasks run simultaneously during the switch, both versions must be able to handle the same APIs and data.

With blue/green deployment, prepare a new environment while keeping the current environment, then switch traffic after validation. With a canary deployment, first send some requests to the updated version and decide whether to switch the remainder based on the results.

When choosing, check the capacity that can be temporarily reserved, the scope of users affected first, and how quickly you can return during an incident. Even with two environments, consider separately whether data written to the shared database is compatible.

example.scenario: The operations team for the order API is releasing a new discount feature. They want to test it first with only 5% of production requests and return the release scope if anything goes wrong.
steps: Verify that the old and new execution environments can handle the same order data.
Send 5% of requests to the updated version and process the remainder in the current environment.
Switch the remainder to the updated version only if the predefined observation period has passed and the criteria are met.
example.outcome: You can limit the impact of an incident while checking the updated version with actual order processing.

misconception.claim: Choosing blue/green deployment lets you return safely without checking the data handled by the application.
misconception.correction: Even if you can switch back to the original environment, recovery is impossible if the previous version cannot read data written by the updated version. Verify shared-data compatibility before switching.

takeaways: Distinguish replacing tasks from switching where users’ traffic is sent.
Confirm that the old and new applications running at the same time can handle the same data.

source.label: Amazon ECS deployment controllers and strategies

sections.title: Set the conditions for expanding the release scope and stopping it
paragraphs: Before starting a canary deployment, define the observation period, required data, and thresholds that stop the release. For an order API, check the order-completion rate in addition to response time and HTTP error rate.

The overall average alone can hide anomalies occurring in the updated version. Separate the metrics for the updated and previous versions and compare them for the same operation. For example, use response time at the 95th percentile to capture slow responses.

When a stop condition is met, do not proceed to the next stage; the responsible person stops the deployment or rolls it back. If the required metrics cannot be obtained, do not expand the release scope until the situation can be confirmed. In CodeDeploy, configured CloudWatch alarms can be used to decide whether to stop a deployment.

example.scenario: After requests to the updated version were set to 5%, its order-completion rate fell below the predefined lower limit.
steps: Do not increase the share of traffic sent to the updated version; stop the rollout.
Check the order-completion rate, error rate, and response time separately for the updated and previous versions.
After confirming that the previous version can handle the shared data, return the traffic according to the procedure.
example.outcome: You can stop the anomaly before it reaches all users and record the scope of the impact and the recovery decision.

misconception.claim: If the monitoring metrics for the updated version cannot be obtained, you can conclude that no anomaly has occurred.
misconception.correction: Determine whether no processing occurred or whether monitoring aggregation stopped. Do not send new traffic until the required metrics can be confirmed.

takeaways: Define monitoring items, the observation period, and stop conditions before release.
Do not rely on the overall average; separately check the updated and previous versions and the application and business results.

source.label: Configuring alarms and rollback in AWS CodeDeploy

sections.title: Choose between rolling back to the previous version and applying a fix
paragraphs: Rolling back means returning to the same configuration as the application before the incident. Use it when the previous version is available and can handle the current data and dependent services. A CodeDeploy rollback redeploys a previously deployed revision.

If the previous version cannot handle the new data format, another option is to release a fix that can read the current data. Decide by comparing the incident impact, the scope that can be rolled back, and the time to recovery, including validation.
In either case, confirm after switching that processing has recovered. Check not only response time but also order creation and lookup, and whether there are duplicate or unprocessed orders.

example.scenario: After releasing an updated version of the order API, an error was found in price calculation. The updated version stores order data in the same format as the previous version.
steps: Stop expanding the release and confirm that the previous version can use the current configuration and data.
Return traffic to the version that was running before the incident.
Execute order creation and lookup, and also check orders saved during the incident and those requiring reprocessing.
example.outcome: You can confirm that order operations recovered, not merely that the application was returned.

misconception.claim: Redeploying the previous version also restores data written during the incident.
misconception.correction: A redeployment of the application restores the execution configuration. Changes to data and processing by external systems must be investigated separately and recovered as necessary.

takeaways: Check compatibility between the data and its dependencies before applying the previous version.
After returning the route, confirm that the actual business operations have recovered.

sections.title: Create a data structure usable by both old and new applications
paragraphs: If you rename database columns while switching the application at the same time, the previous version may be unable to read the old columns during the migration. Add the new columns first and create a state that both the old and new applications can use during the transition.

Migrate the required data and confirm that the updated version processes the new format correctly. Remove the old columns and processing only after there is no longer a possibility of reverting to the previous version. If a data rollback procedure is needed, decide in advance where to restore the data and how to apply it.

When restoring from a backup, simply switching to the restoration target may cause orders placed after the backup was taken to be lost. Validate the restoration procedure, decide how to handle order differences, determine which data is authoritative, and decide when to resume writes.

example.scenario: The order API team changes the column that stores delivery addresses. The old and new applications use the same database for a certain period.
steps: Keep the old column and add a new column.
Read and write values in the application during the migration, and confirm that orders can be handled in both the old and new formats.
Test the recovery procedure, stop the previous version, and then delete the old column.
example.outcome: Even if it becomes necessary to use the previous version during the transition, the system can continue handling order data.

misconception.claim: Publishing the previous version will also restore the database column names and format to those of the previous version.
misconception.correction: The application and database are changed separately. While the previous version may still be used, ensure compatibility of the data structure and prepare restoration as an independent procedure.

takeaways: Add and migrate first, then remove the old structure after the previous version is no longer needed.
Also validate the procedure for handling writes made after the backup.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Database schema changes

questions.title: A method for releasing to a small portion of traffic
